timeline.caption: Point at an element: the tile grows and a card appears at the bottom.
The mouse wheel zooms towards the element under the pointer.
Even close up, the letters on the tiles stay sharp.
Click an element: the camera flies inside.
The Substance in 3D switch shows the simple substance: the iron crystal.
Red rays lead to the elements it forms compounds with. A thick ray means many compounds.
Click a ray, a partner tile or a symbol in the panel: the compounds of the pair line up, the best known first.
Scroll or drag along the ray to move from compound to compound.
The compound card: 3D model, formula, composition, mass, description and sources.
Drag the model to turn it.
To the table, the Esc key or a click on empty space takes you back.
Shift + click picks several elements. On a phone, use Select several.
Show compounds: a cloud of compounds that contain all chosen elements. One orb is one compound.
The filter keeps organic, inorganic substances or minerals only.
Violet orbs are materials predicted by GNoME: found by computation, not by experiment.
Inside an element, Show the violet rays opens the predicted materials.
A predicted material: its unit cell in 3D and its computed properties.
Search: press <kbd>/</kbd>, then type a symbol, a formula or a name in any of three languages.
The How to use button opens a short guide, the data sources and this video.
